System architecture

One plan feeds two models.

01 / Workspace

Plan editor

Turn the event brief into arrival, staffing, process and venue assumptions.

→
02 / Shared data

Versioned JSON plan

The plan schema carries inputs, layout and constraints into each run.

→
03A / In the browser

Agent simulation + 3D replay

A Web Worker generates arrivals and queues. Three.js renders the venue and playback.

03B / Via the Python bridge

Corridor optimization

The bridge sends a busy arrival sample to Doni’s API to compare ticket scan lanes at one entrance.

↶ Back to the plan

The organizer can review an eligible candidate, save a new version and replay the full plan.

06 / Organizer journey

From event input to a revised plan.

A walkthrough of the GBK simulation workspace

  1. 01 / Create an event

    User input

    • Describe the event. Enter the event name, venue and schedule.
    • Enter the initial plan. Add expected attendance, ticket groups and arrival windows as known.
    • Fill in missing details. Add venue and entrance assumptions as they become available.

    Open the draft in the plan editor.

  2. 02 / Define the baseline

    Plan editor

    • Participants: ticket categories, arrival windows and group behavior assumptions.
    • Process: help desk, security, ticket scan and wristband steps.
    • Venue and resources: entrances, staffed lanes, gate hours and walking routes.

    Save a baseline plan version.

  3. 03 / Observe the baseline

    Simulation

    • Agent behavior: generate visitors by category, origin and arrival time.
    • Spatial model: follow origin points and waypoints through the venue, with walking and processing times.
    • 3D replay: follow arrivals, queues and admissions on the GBK map.

    Find an entrance and time window to test.

  4. 04 / Test a change

    Optimization

    • Select a corridor: pick one entrance. OPSIDIO samples a busy arrival wave.
    • Compare scan lanes: review baseline versus candidate queue and wait metrics.
    • Review and apply: save an improving candidate that fits the authored layout as a new version.

    Return to simulation and compare the full run.

↶ Review → save → replay

Keep the baseline, replay the candidate with the same seed, and compare at the same event time.

The GBK plan uses fictional operating assumptions. Live optimization requires the configured server bridge.

07 / From planning assumptions to operational evidence

Rehearse the plan.
Before the crowd arrives.

OPSIDIO is a decision workspace for entrance teams: connect assumptions, rehearse operations, and compare feasible alternatives.

01 / MODEL

Model the entrance

Arrivals, gate allocations, screening, scanning and staffing.

02 / SIMULATE

Inspect the baseline

Find where queues and bottlenecks emerge in the model.

03 / TEST

Test a feasible change

Adjust staffing or gate assumptions within operating constraints.

04 / COMPARE

Compare the outcomes

Inspect waiting, queues, completion and staffing load.

From the planning questions
to the live decision experiment.
